It serves renewable energy (solar, wind and hydro), industrial and specialised applications including furnace and converter duty, selling to private utilities, renewable developers, cement, sugar, steel and hydrocarbon industries, large-scale EPC contractors and power plant developers. The expansion is funded entirely through internal accruals, consistent with the Company's zero-debt balance sheet and substantial cash reserves. risks.note: Movements in the prices of cold-rolled grain-oriented steel and copper can affect profitability. The Company states much of the impact is mitigated through variable pricing contracts linked to the IEEMA index, but the exposure is structural to a transformer manufacturer's cost base.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility in CRGO steel and copper

risks.note: BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single business activity (electric power generation, transmission and distribution) and 100% from a single product line, Power & Distribution Transformers. There is no product or segment diversification to absorb a downturn in the transformer cycle.

Exports contribute 48.31% of total turnover. Global trade tensions, the Middle East conflict from end-February 2026 and associated supply-chain disruptions are explicitly cited as forces reshaping the macro backdrop, and the IMF flags further escalation of trade tensions as a downside risk. A concentrated export book is therefore exposed to events entirely outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: High export dependence and geopolitical/trade disruption

risks.note: Extended lead times for critical inputs and components can influence project timelines, an industry-level challenge that directly affects the Company's ability to convert orders into dispatches.
risks.risk: Supply-chain lead times for critical inputs

risks.note: The shift towards higher-voltage equipment, while positive for value, may continue to influence the pace of order execution in the near term. Sector-level ordering already moderated during FY26 owing primarily to execution-bandwidth constraints and longer lead times for higher-kV equipment. This is directly relevant given the Company's own move into the 220 kV class.
risks.risk: Execution bandwidth as the industry migrates to higher-voltage equipment

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a Risk with negative financial implications, given transformer manufacturing involves heavy equipment, high-voltage testing and material handling. Mitigated through safety protocols, regular training, statutory compliance, continuous monitoring, risk assessments and employee feedback mechanisms.

The Indian rupee depreciated to an all-time low of approximately Rs 95/USD by end-March 2026 on foreign portfolio outflows and market volatility following the Middle East crises, and higher oil and gas import costs are expected to raise inflationary pressures. For an exporter that also imports key inputs, this cuts both ways on realisations and cost.

The BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 28.38% in FY 25-26, broadly in line with 28.57% in FY 24-25 and 24.49% in FY 23-24. Sustained attrition near 28% is a structural human-capital risk for a made-to-order engineering business, even as permanent-worker turnover was nil.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
